STANDARDISATION OF VOLTAGES

"IN electricity supply ... are we content to
potter along towards standardisation of systems
and of voltages little by little and bit by bit at

Electricity Commission, asked this question at the

Centre of the Institution of Electrical Engineers at
Liverpool on November 21st. The rest of his speech
left very little doubt that to tackle the problem in

and economically unsound.

brief_context: Restored the Norman Keep of Cardiff Castle.
brief_extract: Although an entirely modern city of 227,000 inhabitants, whose industrial history dates back only about 90 years, Cardiff's actual history can be traced to the Roman occupation, for remains can still be seen of the original Roman Fortress. After the Norman Conquest another strong fortress was erected to guard the little town, and, thanks to the Marquis of Bute, the owner of Cardiff Castle, this Norman Keep (as it is styled) has been restored to its original form and can be seen within the Castle grounds. With the discovery of the immensely rich South Wales Coalfield came the birth of Cardiff as we know it to-day.

Ancient Greek credited with early observations of electricity.
brief_extract: William Gilbert, his contemporary, had named “ electric,” would, after more than two hundred years, revolutionise the world, and, by bringing us messages over wires or through the air, “ put a girdle round about the earth ” in less than forty minutes. When, in about 600 B.C., Thales of Miletus, one of the Seven Wise Men of Greece, noted that amber, jet, and some other substances had the power, when rubbed, of attracting bits of leaves, straw or feathers, he made the first discovery of electricity. But Thales, the father of Greek philosophy, who even in that remote age could predict an eclipse of the sun, seems to have felt that this observation was of little importance.

brief_context: Roman author who recorded electrical experiments in Natural History.
brief_extract: Certainly none of the ancients suspected the true nature of electricity, nor did they connect the peculiar properties of amber with the lightning flash. Pliny the Elder, a Roman, in his famous “ Natural History,” told of similar experiments to those of Thales, and recorded the painful shocks felt by anybody who touched the curious torpedo-fish. Yet it did not occur to him that both these phenomena had a common cause.

Benjamin Franklin, Volta, Ampère, Michael Faraday,

brief_extract: The Pilchard Inn on the island, with its typical West Country name, dates from 1395, and is electrically lighted from the original ships' lanterns. Chaucer's " Tabard " and Shakespeare's " Mermaid Tavern " recall the rich association with English life of the inn and hostelry. The rafters have echoed with the exploits of highwayman and smuggler—the " Gentleman of the Road " and the " Gentleman of the Sea." They are often found next the village church, as in the old days, when opportunities for obtaining news of the outside world were fewer, assemblies in the church would adjourn to the inn, where travellers from afar sought rest and refreshment, and local gossip was exchanged for " foreign affairs." To-day electricity has transformed some of them, adding greatly to the comforts and taking nothing from the charm and atmosphere.
